claims.statement: A session in gmmff represents a peer-to-peer file and message transfer session between 2-10 peers that is established when peers share a secret code and complete PAKE authentication and WebRTC handshake.

A slot is the server-side representation of a session waiting for peers to join, with lifecycle states: WAITING (StateWaiting), ACTIVE (StateActive), FULL (StateFull), CLOSED (StateClosed) as defined in internal/slot/slot.go.

gmmff uses the CPace PAKE protocol over ristretto255 group to establish a shared secret from a 3-word code, which is used to derive HKDF subkeys for HMAC-signing SDP messages to prevent man-in-the-middle attacks on the signaling server.

Once peers establish a shared secret via PAKE, they create a direct WebRTC data channel encrypted with DTLS 1.3, using SCTP over DTLS for transport, with separate persistent control channel and ephemeral transfer channels per file.
The gmmff wire protocol defines specific binary tags for WebRTC data channel frames (0x01-0x0F) that are frozen and cannot be renumbered without breaking deployed clients.
Any filename arriving from a peer must be processed through the sanitiseName function before touching the filesystem to strip path separators, null bytes, and prevent path traversal attacks.
